topics.title: Vectors, position vectors and direction cosines

learn.hook: 'Go 5 km' is useless to a pilot. 'Go 5 km north-east' is an instruction. That difference between a scalar and a vector is where this chapter begins.
points: Scalars have magnitude only (mass, time, speed, temperature). Vectors have magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force).
A vector is a directed line segment AB with initial point A and terminal point B; its magnitude is the length |AB|.
Position vector of P(x, y, z): OP = xi + yj + zk, with |OP| = √(x² + y² + z²).
If OP makes angles α, β, γ with the x-, y-, z-axes, then l = cos α, m = cos β, n = cos γ are its direction cosines, and l² + m² + n² = 1.
Direction ratios are any numbers a, b, c proportional to l, m, n; for r = ai + bj + ck, l = a/|r|, m = b/|r|, n = c/|r|.

example.q: Find the direction cosines of the vector i + 2j + 2k.

learn.reallife: Air traffic controllers at Delhi airport give each plane a velocity vector: speed plus heading. Two planes with the same speed but different headings are on very different paths.

quiz.q: What is the magnitude of the position vector of P(2, 3, −6)?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to take the square root

quiz.q: What is the direction cosine n (with the z-axis) of the vector 2i − 2j + k?
quiz.mistake: Uses the component itself, forgetting to divide by |r|

quiz.q: A line makes angles 90°, 60° and γ with the x-, y- and z-axes. What is cos²γ?
quiz.explain: cos²90° + cos²60° + cos²γ = 1 ⇒ 0 + 1/4 + cos²γ = 1 ⇒ cos²γ = 3/4.
quiz.mistake: Uses cos 60° instead of cos² 60°

quiz.q: Which are direction cosines of a vector equally inclined to the three axes?
quiz.explain: l = m = n and 3l² = 1, so l = 1/√3 (taking the positive sign).
quiz.mistake: Takes direction ratios 1, 1, 1 as direction cosines

quiz.q: Which of these is a scalar quantity?
quiz.explain: Work is a number (with units) with no direction; the others need a direction.
steps: Scalar: magnitude only; vector: magnitude and direction
Force, displacement and velocity all need a direction
Work done is just a number with units
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything in physics with units is a vector

quiz.q: Which set can be the direction ratios of a line with direction cosines 2/7, 3/7, 6/7?
quiz.explain: Direction ratios are proportional to direction cosines; 4, 6, 12 = 14 × (2/7, 3/7, 6/7).
steps: Direction ratios must be proportional to 2/7, 3/7, 6/7, in the same order
2, 3, 5 is not proportional; 6, 3, 2 is in the wrong order
quiz.mistake: Reorders the numbers, which changes the direction

quiz.q: For any vector, what is l² + m² + n²?
quiz.explain: This identity holds for every set of direction cosines.
steps: l = cos α, m = cos β, n = cos γ for any direction
quiz.mistake: Confuses direction cosines with direction ratios

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): 1, 2, 2 are direction ratios but not direction cosines of a line.
Reason (R): For direction cosines, l² + m² + n² = 1.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: 1 + 4 + 4 = 9 ≠ 1, so they cannot be direction cosines, but any proportional triple can be direction ratios.
steps: R: direction cosines satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1 — true
1² + 2² + 2² = 9 ≠ 1, so 1, 2, 2 are not direction cosines; but they can be direction ratios
So A is true, and R is the reason
Answer: Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.mistake: Treats direction ratios and cosines as the same

teach.ask: Gappu wonders: 'What makes a vector different from a plain number, and what are direction cosines?'
teach.praise: Tweet! A vector has size and direction; its direction cosines are cosines of the angles with the axes, and their squares add to 1!
teach.nudge: What special relation do l, m and n always satisfy?

revise.summary: A vector has magnitude and direction; the position vector of P(x, y, z) is xi + yj + zk with length √(x² + y² + z²). Its direction cosines l, m, n satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1.
focus: Find magnitude and direction cosines of a vector
Use l² + m² + n² = 1 to find a missing angle
Tell direction ratios from direction cosines
traps: Divide components by |r| to get direction cosines
Direction ratios need not satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1
Square the cosines: cos²60° = 1/4

learn.hook: Two cricket fielders running in the same direction at the same speed from different spots have equal velocity vectors, even though they start in different places.
points: Zero (null) vector 0: magnitude zero, initial and terminal points coincide; its direction is not defined (any direction).
Unit vector: magnitude 1; the unit vector along a is â. Coinitial vectors share the same initial point.
Collinear (parallel) vectors lie along the same or parallel lines, whatever their magnitudes or senses.
Equal vectors: same magnitude and same direction, regardless of initial points. Negative of AB is BA, with the same magnitude and opposite direction.
Free vectors can be moved parallel to themselves without change; in this chapter all vectors are free vectors.

example.q: In a square ABCD, classify AB and DC, and AB and CD.
steps: AB and DC have the same length and point the same way, so they are equal vectors.
CD points opposite to AB with the same length, so CD = −AB.
All of them are collinear (parallel) vectors.

learn.reallife: A map app's route is a chain of displacement vectors; sliding one leg of the route parallel to itself does not change that vector, because displacement vectors are free vectors.

games.title: Type check
items: Equal vectors must have the same initial point.
Two collinear vectors always have equal magnitudes.
Collinear vectors may differ in length.
i, j and k are unit vectors.
They have equal length and opposite directions.
The zero vector has a fixed direction.
They are parallel with the same sense.

quiz.q: Which vector is a unit vector?
quiz.mistake: Thinks a vector with entries 1 is automatically a unit vector

quiz.q: In parallelogram ABCD, which pair are equal vectors?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides AB and DC are equal in length and point the same way.
steps: Equal vectors: same length and same direction
In parallelogram ABCD, AB and DC are opposite sides pointing the same way
CD points the opposite way to AB, so CD = −AB
quiz.mistake: Confuses CD with DC

quiz.q: Vectors a and −3a are
quiz.explain: −3a is parallel to a (opposite sense, three times as long).
steps: −3a = (−3) × a: it lies along the same line as a
It is 3 times as long and points the opposite way, so it is not equal to a
quiz.mistake: Thinks opposite direction means not collinear

quiz.q: What is the magnitude of the zero vector?
quiz.explain: The zero vector has length zero.
steps: Zero vector: initial and terminal points coincide
quiz.mistake: Confuses magnitude with direction

quiz.q: Which statement about free vectors is true?
options: They must start at the origin
They can be shifted parallel to themselves without changing
quiz.explain: A free vector is defined only by magnitude and direction, not position.
steps: A free vector is fixed only by magnitude and direction
Its position does not matter, so it can be moved parallel to itself
Answer: They can be shifted parallel to themselves without changing
quiz.mistake: Mixes up free vectors with position vectors

quiz.q: Vectors OA, OB and OC all start at O. They are called
quiz.explain: Coinitial means having the same initial point.
steps: OA, OB, OC all have the same initial point O
Vectors with a common initial point are called coinitial
quiz.mistake: Assumes vectors with a common point must be collinear

quiz.q: Riya walks 4 km west, then 3 km north. What is the magnitude (km) of her displacement vector?
quiz.explain: The two legs are perpendicular, so the magnitude is √(16 + 9) = 5 km.
quiz.mistake: Adds the distances instead of combining the vectors

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): Two vectors having the same magnitude are equal.
Reason (R): Equal vectors have the same magnitude and the same direction.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
quiz.explain: Equality needs the same direction as well; i and j have the same magnitude but are not equal.
steps: R: equal vectors need the same magnitude and the same direction — true
i and j both have magnitude 1 but different directions, so they are not equal
Answer: A is false but R is true
quiz.mistake: Ignores direction when comparing vectors

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is the difference between equal, collinear and negative vectors?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Equal: same size and direction. Collinear: parallel lines. Negative: same size, opposite direction!
teach.nudge: Can two vectors with the same length still be unequal?

revise.summary: Vectors may be zero, unit, coinitial, collinear, equal or negative of each other. Equal vectors need the same magnitude and the same direction; position does not matter for free vectors.
focus: Classify pairs of vectors in figures like parallelograms
Identify unit and zero vectors
Use perpendicular legs to find a displacement
remember: Equal vectors: same magnitude and direction
Collinear: along the same or parallel lines (any sense)
traps: Same magnitude alone does not make vectors equal
CD is not DC: CD = −DC
Opposite direction still counts as collinear

learn.hook: A boat crossing the Ganga while the river pushes it downstream ends up somewhere neither push alone would take it. Vector addition finds where.
points: Triangle law: if a and b are two sides of a triangle in order (head to tail), the third side taken from the start to the end is a + b: AB + BC = AC.
So AB + BC + CA = 0 for any triangle ABC.
Parallelogram law: if a and b are adjacent sides from a common point, the diagonal from that point is a + b.
Properties: a + b = b + a (commutative), (a + b) + c = a + (b + c) (associative), a + 0 = a, a + (−a) = 0.
Triangle inequality: |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|, with equality only when a and b point the same way.

example.q: In triangle ABC, simplify AB + BC + CA.
steps: By the triangle law, AB + BC = AC.

learn.reallife: Pilots flying from Mumbai to Chennai add the plane's air velocity to the wind velocity; the resultant vector is the actual ground track.

games.title: Triangle law
items: Draw vector a from point A to point B
Draw vector b starting at B, ending at C

quiz.q: In triangle ABC, what is AB + BC + CA?
quiz.explain: AB + BC = AC, and AC + CA = 0.
quiz.mistake: Adds magnitudes instead of vectors

quiz.q: In parallelogram ABCD, AB + AD equals
quiz.explain: By the parallelogram law, the diagonal from A is the sum of the adjacent sides from A.
steps: Parallelogram law: sum of adjacent sides from A = diagonal from A
AB + AD = AB + BC = AC (since AD = BC)
quiz.mistake: Picks the other diagonal

quiz.q: If |a| = 3 and |b| = 4, what is the greatest possible value of |a + b|?
quiz.explain: |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b| = 7, with equality when a and b have the same direction.
quiz.mistake: Assumes the vectors are perpendicular

quiz.q: If |a| = 3 and |b| = 4, what is the least possible value of |a + b|?
quiz.explain: The sum is smallest when a and b point in opposite directions: 4 − 3 = 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sum can always be zero

quiz.q: Which property says (a + b) + c = a + (b + c)?
quiz.explain: Associativity means grouping does not matter.
steps: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c): the grouping changes, the order does not
That is the associative law (commutative is a + b = b + a)
quiz.mistake: Confuses associative with commutative

quiz.q: A boat moves at 4 km/h straight across a river flowing at 3 km/h. What is the boat's resultant speed (km/h)?
quiz.explain: The velocities are perpendicular, so |v| = √(16 + 9) = 5.
quiz.mistake: Adds the speeds directly

quiz.q: In triangle ABC, if AB = a and BC = b, then CA equals
quiz.explain: AB + BC + CA = 0, so CA = −(a + b).
quiz.mistake: Forgets the minus sign

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): For any two vectors, |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|.
Reason (R): The length of any side of a triangle is at most the sum of the other two sides.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: a, b and a + b form a triangle (or a straight line), so A follows from the triangle side rule.
steps: R: a side of a triangle ≤ sum of the other two sides — true
a, b and a + b form a triangle (or lie on one line), with |a + b| as the third side
Answer: Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.mistake: Thinks vector sums obey ordinary number addition for lengths

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I add two arrows?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Place them head to tail and join start to end, or use the parallelogram's diagonal. Arrow arithmetic!
teach.nudge: Where does the second arrow start in the triangle law?

revise.summary: Vectors add head to tail (triangle law) or along the diagonal of a parallelogram. Addition is commutative and associative, and |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|.
focus: Simplify sums like AB + BC + CA
Use the parallelogram law
Find the largest and smallest possible |a + b|
remember: AB + BC = AC; AB + BC + CA = 0
traps: Don't add magnitudes when adding vectors
Least |a + b| is ||a| − |b||, not always 0
Keep the minus sign in CA = −(a + b)

learn.hook: Every vector in space is just a mix of three building blocks: i, j and k. Know the mix, and you know everything about the vector.
points: λa has magnitude |λ||a|; it points along a if λ > 0 and opposite if λ < 0. The unit vector along a is â = a/|a|.
r = xi + yj + zk: x, y, z are scalar components and xi, yj, zk are vector components.
Operations are componentwise; a = b exactly when corresponding components are equal.
a and b are collinear ⇔ b = λa for some scalar λ ⇔ their components are proportional.
Vector joining P(x₁, y₁, z₁) to Q(x₂, y₂, z₂): PQ = (x₂ − x₁)i + (y₂ − y₁)j + (z₂ − z₁)k.

example.q: Find a vector of magnitude 14 in the direction of 2i − 3j + 6k.

learn.reallife: A delivery drone's flight can be described leg by leg with components east, north and up; adding the components gives the drone's net position.

items.q: x-component of PQ for P(2, 3, 0), Q(−1, −2, −4)
x if xi + 2j − zk = 3i + yj + k
z if xi + 2j − zk = 3i + yj + k

games.title: Collinear or not?
items: The second is −2 times the first.
i + j and i − j are collinear.
−a has the same magnitude as a.
a/|a| is a unit vector for every non-zero a.

quiz.q: Find the unit vector in the direction of a = 2i + 3j + k.
quiz.mistake: Divides by |a|² instead of |a|

quiz.q: P(2, 3, 0) and Q(−1, −2, −4). What is PQ?
steps: PQ = OQ − OP = (x₂ − x₁)i + (y₂ − y₁)j + (z₂ − z₁)k
quiz.mistake: Subtracts Q from P instead of P from Q

quiz.q: Find a vector of magnitude 21 in the direction of 2i − 3j + 6k.
quiz.explain: |2i − 3j + 6k| = 7, so multiply the unit vector by 21: 3(2i − 3j + 6k).
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the vector itself by 21

quiz.q: If a = 2i − 3j + 4k and b = −4i + λj − 8k are collinear, what is λ?
quiz.explain: b = −2a requires λ = −2 × (−3) = 6.
quiz.mistake: Gets the sign wrong

quiz.q: If xi + 2j − zk = 3i + yj + k, what is x + y + z?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the minus sign on z

quiz.q: Show A(1, 2, 7), B(2, 6, 3), C(3, 10, −1) are collinear. Which fact proves it?
options: A, B, C have positive x-coordinates
quiz.explain: AB and BC are parallel and share point B, so A, B, C lie on one line.
steps: AB = BC, so AC = AB + BC = 2AB; parallel with common point B ⇒ collinear
Answer: AB = BC = i + 4j − 4k, so AC = 2AB
quiz.mistake: Uses equal magnitudes, which does not show the same line

quiz.q: What are the scalar components of the vector joining A(1, −1, 2) to B(4, 3, 2)?
quiz.explain: AB = (4 − 1)i + (3 + 1)j + (2 − 2)k = 3i + 4j. Scalar components are 3, 4, 0.
quiz.mistake: Gives vector components when scalar components were asked

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): −2a is a vector of magnitude 2|a| opposite to a.
Reason (R): For a scalar λ, |λa| = |λ||a|, and λa reverses direction when λ < 0.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: With λ = −2, |λa| = 2|a| and the direction reverses.
steps: R: |λa| = |λ||a|, and λ < 0 reverses direction — true
Answer: Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.mistake: Thinks a negative scalar makes the magnitude negative

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I find a vector of length 14 pointing the same way as 2i − 3j + 6k?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Divide by its magnitude to get the unit vector, then multiply by 14. Same direction, new length!
teach.nudge: What do you first divide the vector by?

revise.summary: λa scales the length by |λ| and reverses direction when λ < 0. Vectors are added, compared and scaled componentwise, and two vectors are collinear exactly when their components are proportional.
focus: Find a unit vector and a vector of given magnitude
Find PQ from two points
Test collinearity by proportional components
traps: Subtract P from Q for PQ, not Q from P
Scalar components are numbers; vector components include i, j, k
Multiply the unit vector, not the vector, by the required magnitude

learn.hook: Where exactly is the point two-thirds of the way from Pune to Mumbai on a straight road? The section formula answers instantly in vector form.
points: If P and Q have position vectors a and b, the point R dividing PQ internally in the ratio m : n has position vector (mb + na)/(m + n).
Externally in the ratio m : n (m ≠ n): (mb − na)/(m − n).
Mid-point of PQ: (a + b)/2 (internal division with m = n = 1).
Centroid of a triangle with vertices a, b, c: (a + b + c)/3.
Remember the 'cross' pattern: m goes with b (the far end), n with a (the near end).

example.q: OP = i + 2j − k and OQ = −i + j + k. Find the point R dividing PQ internally in the ratio 2 : 1.

learn.reallife: To place a station two-thirds of the way along a straight stretch of track between two points, a planner can use exactly this section formula.

games.title: External division of PQ in 2 : 1 (P = i + 2j − k, Q = −i + j + k)

quiz.q: What is the position vector of the mid-point of a and b?
quiz.explain: Internal division with m = n = 1 gives (a + b)/2.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of adding

quiz.q: P = i + 2j − k and Q = −i + j + k. R divides PQ externally in the ratio 2 : 1. What is OR?
steps: External: OR = (m OQ − n OP)/(m − n) with m = 2, n = 1
quiz.mistake: Uses the internal formula instead

quiz.q: A has position vector 2i + j − k and B has 4i − 3j + 5k. What is the x-component of the mid-point of AB?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide by 2

quiz.q: Find the position vector of the point dividing a = 2i + j and b = 5i + 7j internally in 1 : 2. What is its y-component?
quiz.mistake: Pairs m with a instead of b

quiz.q: The centroid of the triangle with vertices i, j and k has position vector
quiz.explain: Centroid = (a + b + c)/3.
steps: a = i, b = j, c = k
quiz.mistake: Uses 1/2 as for a mid-point

quiz.q: In the internal section formula (mb + na)/(m + n), which ratio does R divide PQ in, with P at a and Q at b?
quiz.explain: R is closer to P when m < n; the weights cross over to the far end.
steps: In (mb + na)/(m + n), m is the weight on b (the end Q) and n on a (the end P)
This gives the point R with PR : RQ = m : n
quiz.mistake: Reverses the meaning of the ratio

quiz.q: For external division in the ratio 3 : 1 of a = i and b = 2i, what is the resulting vector?
quiz.mistake: Uses m + n in the denominator

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): The mid-point formula is a special case of the internal section formula.
Reason (R): Taking m = n = 1 in (mb + na)/(m + n) gives (a + b)/2.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: Equal ratio 1 : 1 gives the mid-point, which R computes.
steps: R: m = n = 1 in (mb + na)/(m + n) gives (b + a)/2 — true
So the mid-point formula comes from the section formula: A is true because of R
Answer: Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.mistake: Treats the mid-point formula as unrelated

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I find the point dividing a line segment in the ratio m : n using vectors?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Internal: (mb + na)/(m + n). External: (mb − na)/(m − n). Cross the weights and divide!
teach.nudge: Which position vector does m multiply, a or b?

revise.summary: The point dividing PQ internally in m : n is (mb + na)/(m + n), and externally (mb − na)/(m − n). The mid-point is (a + b)/2 and the centroid is (a + b + c)/3.
focus: Apply internal and external section formulas
Find mid-points and centroids
Pair m with the far end b
traps: Don't pair m with a
Use m − n, not m + n, for external division
Centroid uses 1/3, not 1/2

learn.hook: Pull a cart with a rope at an angle and only part of your force moves it forward. The dot product measures exactly that useful part.
points: a · b = |a||b| cos θ, where θ (0 ≤ θ ≤ π) is the angle between a and b. The result is a scalar.
Properties: a · b = b · a, a · (b + c) = a · b + a · c, (λa) · b = λ(a · b).
i · i = j · j = k · k = 1 and i · j = j · k = k · i = 0. So (a₁i + a₂j + a₃k) · (b₁i + b₂j + b₃k) = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃.
Angle: cos θ = (a · b)/(|a||b|).
a ⊥ b ⇔ a · b = 0 (for non-zero vectors). a · a = |a|².

example.q: Find the angle between a = i + j and b = j + k.

learn.reallife: In physics, work = F · d. A porter at a railway station carrying luggage horizontally does no work against gravity, since force and displacement are perpendicular.

games.title: Dot product facts
items: If a · b = 0 for non-zero a, b, they are perpendicular.
i and j are perpendicular, so i · j = 0.
If a · b < 0, the angle between them is obtuse.
cos θ < 0 means θ is between π/2 and π.

quiz.q: Find (2i + 3j + k) · (i − j + 2k).
quiz.mistake: Drops a sign

quiz.q: For which λ are 2i + λj + k and i − 2j + 3k perpendicular?
quiz.mistake: Makes a sign slip solving 5 − 2λ = 0

quiz.q: Find cos θ for the angle between i − 2j + 3k and 3i − 2j + k.
quiz.explain: Dot = 3 + 4 + 3 = 10, each magnitude √14, cos θ = 10/14 = 5/7.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that (−2)(−2) = +4

quiz.q: |a| = √3, |b| = 2 and a · b = √6. What is the angle between a and b?
quiz.mistake: Simplifies √6/√3 wrongly

quiz.q: What is i · (j × k)?
quiz.explain: j × k = i, and i · i = 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every product of different unit vectors is 0

quiz.q: If a · b = 0 and a, b are non-zero, what is the angle between them?
quiz.explain: cos θ = 0 gives θ = π/2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a zero dot product means parallel vectors

quiz.q: Which pair of vectors is perpendicular?
options: i + j − k and 2i − j + k
steps: Answer: i + j − k and 2i − j + k
quiz.mistake: Checks only two components

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): For non-zero vectors, a · b = |a||b| exactly when a and b point in the same direction.
Reason (R): cos θ = 1 only when θ = 0.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.explain: a · b = |a||b| cos θ equals |a||b| only if cos θ = 1, i.e. θ = 0.
steps: a · b = |a||b| ⇔ cos θ = 1 ⇔ θ = 0 (R, true for 0 ≤ θ ≤ π)
θ = 0 means same direction, so R explains A
Answer: Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.mistake: Thinks the dot product equals the product of magnitudes for any angle

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I find the angle between two vectors?'
teach.praise: Chirp! cos θ = (a · b)/(|a||b|). Multiply matching components, add, divide by the lengths!
teach.nudge: Which formula links the dot product with the angle?

revise.summary: a · b = |a||b| cos θ is a scalar, and in components it is a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃. Non-zero vectors are perpendicular exactly when a · b = 0.
focus: Compute dot products in components
Find the angle between two vectors
Find an unknown that makes vectors perpendicular
remember: a · b = |a||b| cos θ = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃
i · i = 1, i · j = 0; a · a = |a|²
traps: (−2)(−2) = +4: watch signs
A zero dot product means perpendicular, not parallel
The dot product is a number, not a vector

learn.hook: A wind of 20 km/h blows at an angle to a runway. How much of it is a headwind? That is the projection of the wind vector on the runway.
points: Projection of a on b = (a · b)/|b| = a · b̂. Its vector form is ((a · b)/|b|²) b.
The projection is positive if the angle is acute and negative if obtuse.
|a + b|² = |a|² + 2a · b + |b|², |a − b|² = |a|² − 2a · b + |b|², and (a + b) · (a − b) = |a|² − |b|².
Cauchy–Schwarz inequality: |a · b| ≤ |a||b|. Triangle inequality: |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|.
If |a + b| = |a − b|, then a · b = 0, so a ⊥ b.

Assertion (A): |a · b| ≤ |a||b| for all vectors a and b.

A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.explain: |a · b| = |a||b||cos θ| ≤ |a||b| because |cos θ| ≤ 1.
steps: a · b = |a||b| cos θ ⇒ |a · b| = |a||b||cos θ|
So |a · b| ≤ |a||b|: A follows from R
Answer: Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.mistake: Does not link the inequality to the cosine bound

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What does the projection of one vector on another mean?'
teach.praise: Tweet! It is the shadow of a along b: (a · b)/|b|. Dot, then divide by b's length!

revise.summary: The projection of a on b is (a · b)/|b|. Expansions like |a ± b|² = |a|² ± 2a · b + |b|² and (a + b) · (a − b) = |a|² − |b|² solve many magnitude problems.
focus: Find the projection of one vector on another
Use dot product identities to find magnitudes
Handle a + b + c = 0 type problems
remember: Projection of a on b = (a · b)/|b|
traps: Divide by |b| (the vector projected on), not |a|
Take the square root at the end when |x| is asked
Don't forget cross terms when expanding

learn.hook: Tighten a bolt with a spanner: the turning effect points along the bolt, perpendicular to both the spanner and your push. That direction is a cross product.
points: a × b = |a||b| sin θ n̂, where n̂ is the unit vector perpendicular to both, chosen by the right-hand rule. The result is a vector.
Anti-commutative: a × b = −(b × a). Distributive: a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c. a × a = 0.
i × j = k, j × k = i, k × i = j; and j × i = −k, k × j = −i, i × k = −j; i × i = j × j = k × k = 0.
Component form: a × b = |i j k; a₁ a₂ a₃; b₁ b₂ b₃| (a 3 × 3 determinant).
Non-zero a and b are parallel ⇔ a × b = 0. (The scalar triple product is not in the current CBSE syllabus.)
learn.reallife: Torque τ = r × F decides how a wind turbine in Tamil Nadu's Muppandal wind farm spins: only the force component perpendicular to the blade turns it.

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): a × b = −(b × a).
Reason (R): Swapping a and b reverses the right-hand-rule direction while keeping |a||b| sin θ the same.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: Same magnitude, opposite normal direction: so b × a = −(a × b).
steps: |b × a| = |b||a| sin θ = |a × b|: same magnitude
Right-hand rule from b to a gives the opposite normal direction
So b × a = −(a × b): R explains A
Answer: Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.mistake: Thinks the cross product is commutative like the dot product

teach.ask: Gappu flaps: 'How is the cross product different from the dot product?'

revise.summary: a × b = |a||b| sin θ n̂ is a vector perpendicular to both a and b, found by a 3 × 3 determinant. It is anti-commutative, and non-zero vectors are parallel exactly when a × b = 0.
focus: Compute a × b by the determinant
Use |a × b| = |a||b| sin θ
Find unknowns from a × b = 0
remember: i × j = k, j × k = i, k × i = j; reversed order gives the negative
traps: Don't forget the minus on the j term of the determinant
Use sin θ, not cos θ, for |a × b|
k × j = −i, not i

topics.title: Using the cross product: perpendicular vectors and areas

learn.hook: Need the area of a triangular plot from three GPS points in 3D? One cross product and a half do it.
points: A unit vector perpendicular to both a and b: ±(a × b)/|a × b|.
Area of a parallelogram with adjacent sides a and b: |a × b|.
Area of a triangle with sides a and b from one vertex: (1/2)|a × b|.
For a parallelogram given by its diagonals d₁ and d₂, area = (1/2)|d₁ × d₂|.
To find a vector satisfying given conditions, write it as xi + yj + zk and use the dot or cross product conditions to form equations.

revise.summary: (a × b)/|a × b| is a unit vector perpendicular to both a and b. |a × b| is the area of the parallelogram on a and b, and half of it is the area of the triangle.

Find areas of parallelograms and triangles
